title: Mt. Diablo Boulevard Corridor Multi-Modal Mobility Plan (M3)
description: Umbrella 20-year multimodal mobility and public-realm framework for Downtown Lafayette (Mt. Diablo Blvd between Acalanes Rd and Pleasant Hill Rd, including BART and commercial core). Guides alignment across concurrent downtown mobility efforts. Advisory input via Multi-Modal Mobility Advisory Committee (~18–24 month term).
location_name: Downtown Lafayette / Mt. Diablo Blvd corridor
notes: Staff report 2026-09-21 MMMAC Meeting #1 (Patrick Golier). Planned MMMAC touchpoints: Fall 2026, Winter 2027, Spring 2027, Summer 2027, Fall 2027

title: BART Station Access & Circulation Study
description: Identify multi-modal access improvements within ½ mile of Lafayette BART; support MTC Transit-Oriented Communities policy. Parallel to M3.
notes: From Attachment 2 (Apr 20 2026 TCC staff report) in MMMAC 5A packet.

title: Aqueduct Pathway – Design (Dolores Dr to Pleasant Hill Rd)
description: Design for Aqueduct Pathway segment between Dolores Drive and Pleasant Hill Road.

title: Aqueduct Pathway – Construction (Dolores Drive to BART)
description: Construct key Aqueduct Pathway segment supporting non-auto access to BART and downtown.
funding_note: Secured from multiple sources totaling $4.15 million; construction phase FY2029

title: BART Town Center Pathway & Bike Station Project
description: Improve bicycle parking, pedestrian connectivity, and public realm near Lafayette BART.
funding_note: Fully funded from multiple sources totaling $3.98 million

title: Connecting Lafayette Project (School Street / Topper Lane)
description: Construct separated Class I pedestrian and bicycle facilities on School Street and Topper Lane connecting neighborhoods, schools, and downtown.
funding_note: Fully funded from multiple sources totaling $4.42 million
notes: Also called Downtown Pathways and Schools Safety Project in M3 presentation.

title: Smart Signals Project
description: Upgraded signal technology for coordination, traffic flow, and safer operations for all users.

title: Downtown Parking Management Study (implementation)
description: Update parking and curb management strategies; study adoption anticipated 1st half 2026; City advancing strategy implementation.
